prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: an arrears payment plan. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"When a member has an arrears payment plan, I check whether the regular instalment is affordable on the current verified income before I treat the account as stable."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the plan has been kept to for several months with no missed payments, I am more comfortable counting it as evidence of recovery than as a fresh arrears event."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the plan is due to end soon, I still confirm the contractual mortgage payment is sustainable on its own, not just the combined plan payment."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I see a plan that is very small compared with the main payment, I prefer to understand what caused the shortfall rather than assume it is immaterial."},{"type":"observation","content":"When arrears started after a temporary shock such as a change in hours or a one-off expense, a documented payment plan often points to a lower ongoing risk than repeated unexplained arrears."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the member is already on a plan, I look for other signs of pressure such as overdraft reliance, missed credit commitments or multiple recent arrangements before I make a decision."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the plan was agreed with the lender and is being followed exactly, it usually tells me more than a member’s verbal assurance that they are managing the account."},{"type":"fact","content":"When considering a remortgage, I make sure the new lender’s affordability view would still hold if the arrears plan ended and the account reverted to the full payment."},{"type":"preference","content":"When there have been repeated arrears plans over a short period, I prefer a cautious view, because that pattern usually means the underlying budget is still fragile."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the plan is supported by clear evidence of improved income or reduced committed spending, I am more likely to treat it as a workable bridge back to normal payments."}]}
